content:
maya: Hey folks — running into a weird edge on the Android sample app. Intermittent 401s when Retrofit retries are enabled. Not the usual token-refresh loop, looks tied to Moshi/OkHttp request body reuse.

danw: hmmm. can you paste the authenticator/interceptor chain?

maya: sure. simplified:
```kotlin
class TokenAuthenticator: Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    val token = TokenStore.refresh() // suspending via runBlocking in my sample
    return response.request.newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
      .build()
  }
}

val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator())
  .addInterceptor { chain ->
    val req = chain.request()
    val newReq = req.newBuilder()
      .header("X-Client", "android-sample")
      .build()
    chain.proceed(newReq)
  }
  .build()
```

maya: behavior: first failed call -> authenticator refreshes and returns new request. But sometimes the retried request body is empty (POST with JSON body), server complains and returns 401 again. After 2-3 loops app hits our retry limit and fails.

rafael: I think OkHttp will only buffer the request body for retries if it's repeatable (i.e., not streaming). Are you using Moshi converter which wraps a Buffer?

maya: using MoshiConverterFactory with Retrofit 2.9 + coroutines adapter. The request body is created by Retrofit from the data class. Most times it works, but on cold device (low memory) it seems body becomes consumed.

elena: also check that your interceptor doesn't call request.body?.contentLength() in a way that consumes it. And if you're reading request.body as string anywhere for logging that will eat it.

maya: good call — we do have a debug interceptor that logs body: `val body = request.body?.buffer?.readUtf8()` — oof. I guess that will drain buffer on some implementations.

danw: yup. Another pattern: use a logging Interceptor that uses cloneable sinks or only logs for idempotent methods. Or make the body buffered (RequestBody.create with a byte[]).

maya: quick repro: disable the debug body logging + add `.retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` -> fewer loops. So it seems double-consumption + retry leads to empty body.

rafael: Also be careful with calling suspending refresh inside Authenticator with runBlocking — that can deadlock with dispatcher if refresh uses same threadpool. Use a synchronous refresh path or a refresh queue outside the authenticator.

maya: agreed. I rewrote TokenStore.refresh() to use a synchronous HTTP client separate from Retrofit and removed runBlocking and logging. That fixed the flakiness in local tests. But still want to document this in the sample app.

elena: can you add a note to the Android sample README about: 1) avoid consuming request bodies in interceptors; 2) use repeatable RequestBody for retries; 3) don't block dispatchers in Authenticator.

maya: will do. also adding a small util to wrap RequestBody in a buffered variant for POSTs in sample.

android-ci-bot: CI build for android/sample-app #482 passed — tests cover token refresh scenario (mock server) :white_check_mark:

danw: maybe add a tiny integration test that asserts POST body is resent after authenticator runs (mockwebserver can check recorded requests).

maya: good idea — I'll add a test and open a PR.

rafael: thanks for debugging this — subtle interplay of logging, body buffering, and auth retries is easy to miss on Android.

maya: PR filed: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/android-samples/pulls/123

elena: tagging docs folks to update onboarding guide: @docs-team pls note Retrofit/OkHttp caveats for token refresh patterns. :memo:

maya: thanks all :raised_hands:
